exact_source_lines.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In
the point/projective-line geometry with $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_2=\mathbb P^1$,
$d_1=0$, $d_2=1$ and $L_1=k$, $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], let
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let
$\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation
$R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by
$1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then
$\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the
correspondence isomorphism of
[[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has
$[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental
class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the
point corner gives its generator.

1.1 The geometry and the cohomology of the projective line. The fiber products are $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathbb P^1$. By [F3] its Schubert CW structure has one $0$-cell and one $2$-cell, so the cellular cochain complex is $k\oplus k[-2]$. By [F4] it computes singular cohomology, and [F6] identifies this with constant-sheaf cohomology. Choosing cocycles representing the two generators gives a quasi-isomorphism $k\oplus k[-2]\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$. Hence $L_2\simeq k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ and $L_1=k$. [F3, F4, F6, algebra]

2.1 The two classes and their composites. The unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes the degree-zero summand, generating $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)=k$. Evaluation at a point projects to that summand; its shift $\beta:L_2\to k[1]$ generates $\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_2,L_1)=k$, since $\operatorname{Hom}(k[-2],k)=0$. Therefore $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$. The reverse composite $\alpha[1]\circ\beta$ is also nonzero: it is the projector of $L_2=k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ onto $k[1]$, and is neither zero nor $\operatorname{id}_{L_2}$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The convolution check. Apply [F2] with $(i,j,k)=(1,2,1)$ and degrees $r=-1$, $s=1$ to the composable pair $\alpha:L_1\to L_2[r]$ and $\beta:L_2\to L_1[s]$: since $\beta[r]\circ\alpha=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ by step 2.1, the product theorem gives $\Phi_{11}^{0}(\operatorname{id}_k)=\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)*\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)$, so $\alpha*\beta=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention, and the right-hand side is the convolution product of [F1]. The corner degrees are $d_1+d_2-r=2$ for $\alpha$ and $d_2+d_1-s=0$ for $\beta$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 The geometric product. The adjunction chain of [F1] sends $\alpha$ to $\operatorname{id}_{k_{\mathbb P^1}}$, hence to the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]$. Write $i:\mathrm{pt}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^1$ for the evaluation point. Evaluation is the global-sections image of $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k$, and its adjoint under $R\Gamma\dashv a^!$, $a:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$, is the composite $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k=i_*i^!\omega_{\mathbb P^1}\to\omega_{\mathbb P^1}$, with the last arrow the proper trace. Thus $\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)=i_*[\mathrm{pt}]$ with coefficient $+1$. Geometrically $\mathbb P^1\times\{i\}$ meets the middle diagonal of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ transversely at $(i,i)$; the map from its tangent line to the complex normal line of the diagonal is an isomorphism, preserving the real orientation. The positive Thom cap of [F5] therefore gives that point with multiplicity $+1$, and proper pushforward to $Z_{11}=\mathrm{pt}$ gives $[\mathrm{pt}]$. This computes $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$, with middle degree drop $2$ and no permutation sign, agreeing with step 3.1. It verifies a transverse instance of the calculus, not its general nontransverse case. AC is inherited through [A1]. [A1, F1, F2, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

selected_candidates.diagram_kind: Two-panel derived composition and correspondence-intersection diagram.
selected_candidates.source_claim: For E=X1=pt and X2=P1, the unit alpha:k→RΓ(P1,k) and point evaluation beta:RΓ(P1,k)[1]→k[1] satisfy source-first alpha*beta=beta[-1]∘alpha=id_k; geometrically P1×{i} meets the middle diagonal at (i,i) with positive complex orientation and pushes to [pt].
selected_candidates.why_warranted: The example contrasts source-first convolution with reverse composition and connects the derived maps to an oriented geometric intersection. A paired diagram can make direction and shifts visible while keeping the two conventions distinct.
concrete_content_to_draw_or_check: Panel A: label a:P1→pt and i:pt→P1 with the correct arrow directions; show L1=k and L2=RΓ(P1,k)[1].

Show alpha:L1→L2[-1] (equivalently the unshifted unit into RΓ(P1,k)) and beta:L2→L1[1], with shift-correct composite beta[-1]∘alpha=id_k; separately label alpha[1]∘beta as the nonzero projector on k[1] in L2=k[1]⊕k[-1].
Panel B: in P1×P1, show P1×{i} and the middle diagonal crossing transversely at (i,i), label the complex-normal orientation as positive, then show proper pushforward to Z11=pt yielding [pt].
correctness_checks: Do not reverse i:pt→P1 or confuse it with a:P1→pt.
Keep Ext grading and shifted source/target of alpha and beta consistent; distinguish beta[-1]∘alpha from alpha[1]∘beta.
Place the intersection in P1×P1 at (i,i); check tangent-to-normal map preserves complex orientation and coefficient is +1.
Mark proper pushforward to the pt corner and middle degree drop 2.
selected_candidates.why_not_confirmed: This is an optional explanatory diagram; the text gives the maps, composites, orientation, and pushforward, with no defect identified.

exact_source_lines.text: Let $\kappa$ be antidominant and let $\alpha$ be a simple root with
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$. Put
$p_\alpha:X=G/B\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$, a Zariski-locally trivial
$\mathbb P^1$-bundle, and let $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\beta\in\Phi^+}\beta$.
Use the partial TDO $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ and pullback module
$p_\alpha^\dagger N$ defined in
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]. For every coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$:
1. $R^q p_{\alpha*}M=0$ for every $q>0$;
2. $p_{\alpha*}M=0$ if and only if there is a coherent
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$ with
$$M\cong\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N,$$
where $N\cong p_{\alpha*}(\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M)$; this determines $N$ up to canonical isomorphism.
[F1] The projection is a Zariski-locally trivial $\mathbb P^1$-bundle;
on product charts its TDO has the singular rank-one relative factor.
The ordinary inverse image of a base module has relative factor
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}$, and $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ has relative factor
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$
([[thm-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection-is-p1-bundle]],
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]).
[F2] For a coherent product differential module on $\mathbb P^1\times U$
with singular relative factor $D_0=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O(-1))$,
all positive higher direct images to $U$ vanish. Its direct image is zero
if and only if it is $\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes N$ for a coherent base-TDO
module $N$, recovered as the direct image after tensoring by
$\mathcal O(1)$. The canonical evaluation is compatible with the differential
transition maps and glues
([[lem-pa36-relative-p1-singular-kernel]]).

2.1 Suppose $p_{\alpha*}M=0$. On a product chart, [F2] gives the canonical differential-module isomorphism $M=\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes N$, with $N=p_{\alpha*}(\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M)$ in that chart's partial TDO convention. The inverse image in [F1] has relative structure-sheaf factor, so this is precisely the displayed form $\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N$. The proof of [F2] makes its evaluation natural in all commuting base operators; on overlaps it is intertwined by the chain rule and the partial TDO cocycle in [F1]. Thus the base actions glue on the stated direct image and the local isomorphisms glue to the asserted global one. Coherence of $N$ is part of [F2], not an inference from $\mathcal O_X$-coherence of $M$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Conversely, the displayed form has local relative factor $\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes N$ by [F1], whose direct image is zero by [F2]; hence $p_{\alpha*}M=0$ globally. Tensoring this form by $\mathcal O_X(-\rho)$ and applying $p_{\alpha*}$ recovers $N$, since $p_{\alpha*}p_\alpha^\dagger N=N$. The same identity proves uniqueness up to the recovered canonical isomorphism. This proves both directions and all higher-image assertions; no rank-one classification is left as a source-only premise. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

selected_candidates.diagram_kind: Rank-one P1-bundle projection and fiberwise direct-image / twist-recovery diagram.
selected_candidates.source_claim: For the minimal-parabolic P1-bundle p_alpha:X→X_alpha, higher direct images of coherent D_kappa modules vanish; p_{alpha*}M=0 exactly for M≅O_X(rho)⊗p_alpha†N, with N recovered as p_{alpha*}(O_X(-rho)⊗M). Fiberwise O_X(rho) has relative O_P1(-1).
selected_candidates.why_warranted: The criterion translates a fiberwise relative O(-1) kernel into a global partial-TDO pullback and recovers N by the opposite twist. A small bundle/fiber diagram could make the roles of p_alpha, the relative line bundle, and the recovery pushforward easier to distinguish.
concrete_content_to_draw_or_check: Draw p_alpha:X=G/B→X_alpha=G/P_alpha as a locally trivial P1-bundle, with a fiber P1 over a base chart U.
On that fiber label the untwisted inverse-image relative factor O_P1 and the O_X(rho) relative factor O_P1(-1); show O(-1)⊠N as the zero-pushforward case.
Show p_{alpha*}M=0 iff M≅O_X(rho)⊗p_alpha†N, and the recovery arrow N≅p_{alpha*}(O_X(-rho)⊗M).
If showing gluing, label compatible TDO transition maps; do not depict X as globally a product.
correctness_checks: Orient p_alpha from X to X_alpha and keep N a module over the partial TDO on X_alpha.
Use relative O_P1(-1) for O_X(rho), and relative O_P1 for the ordinary inverse image; do not interchange rho and -rho.
Show the recovery twist O_X(-rho) before applying p_{alpha*}.
Indicate that P1×U is only a local product chart; the gluing uses compatible transition maps.
selected_candidates.why_not_confirmed: The statement and proof already specify the P1-bundle, fiber twist, pushforward criterion, and canonical recovery. A diagram is optional and no mathematical or rendering error is alleged.
